### `CreatedAt` (decorator)

Stamp the property server-side with `datetime()` once on create (NTS-165): the database clock writes it, so clocks never drift across clients. Stack it with a type decorator (e.g. `@DateTime()`) for a declared type. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.

### `SoftDelete` (decorator)

Declarative soft delete (NTS-510): mark the model so delete() stamps a label + deletedAt instead of DETACH DELETE, and every standard read (find / findAll / all / projections / repository reads) filters the label out. Restore with restore(); hard-delete with delete(force). The label defaults to 'Deleted'; the stamp property is `deletedAt` (declared implicitly, server-stamped with datetime()).

_source: decorators/node/soft-delete.decorator.ts_

On a relationship entity: the property holding the node at the relationship's start.

### `Time` (decorator)

Register a time property.

_source: decorators/node/time.decorator.ts_

### `TransformConfig` (interface)

Property value transforms (NTS-449): user-supplied value mappers applied on the write and read paths. `in` converts a user value into its stored form before validation on every write path (create / update / merge / bulk); `out` converts the stored form back at hydration. Both may be async on the write path — `out` must be synchronous, hydration is synchronous. Failures surface as a NeodeError naming the model and property.

_source: meta/schema-definition.interface.ts_

### `Unique` (decorator)

Mark the property as unique: installSchema() backs it with a uniqueness constraint, and merge() treats races on it as constraint violations. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.

_source: decorators/node/unique.decorator.ts_

### `UpdatedAt` (decorator)

Stamp the property server-side with `datetime()` on create and on every write (NTS-165): the database clock writes it, so clocks never drift across clients. Stack it with a type decorator (e.g. `@DateTime()`) for a declared type. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.

_source: decorators/node/updated-at.decorator.ts_

### `Uuid` (decorator)

Register a UUID property: validated as a UUID string, defaulting to a random UUID v4 on create (an explicit `config.default` wins).

_source: decorators/node/uuid.decorator.ts_

### `ValidationRules` (interface)

Validation rules accepted on a property definition (neode's Joi rule names, ported in src/validation/rule-table.ts). Every non-metamodel key of a map-schema property definition travels to the validator as a rule (mergeProperty persists it via PropertySchema#setRules), so these are the keys the published map API accepts alongside the structural options. Rules are applied on top of the property's base type: a rule the base type does not support throws at validation time (rule-table's failUnsupported), and boolean rules must be exactly `true`.

_source: meta/schema-definition.interface.ts_

### `Vector` (decorator)

Declare a vector index over the property (NTS-447): `installSchema()` creates the index with the deterministic `vectorIndexName()` naming, `dropSchema()` drops it, and `knn()` searches it. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.

_source: decorators/node/vector.decorator.ts_

### `VectorConfig` (interface)

Vector index declaration for a property (NTS-447): installing the schema creates a Neo4j vector index over the property (dropped by `dropSchema()`), and `knn()` searches it. `dimensions` must match the embedding model; `similarityFunction` defaults to 'cosine'.

_source: meta/schema-definition.interface.ts_

### `Version` (decorator)

Optimistic locking (NTS-158): mark the property as the model's version — stamped 0 on create, incremented by 1 on every write addressed to the node, and checked with `WHERE n.version = $expected` when the instance carries the version it was hydrated with. A mismatch (the node changed underneath you) throws `OptimisticLockError` — reload the entity and retry. Version is per node only: writes reached through another node's save (nested relationship targets) never bump it. Stack it with a type decorator (e.g. `@Number()`) for a declared type. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked.

_source: decorators/node/version.decorator.ts_

### `WithMethods` (type)

Type helper for entity instances: `WithMethods<Person>` adds the instance methods to a user class. Runtime works on hydrated instances regardless — this is only for type-checking, since declaration merging onto arbitrary user classes is not possible.

_source: entity-methods.ts_

## Querying

Query builder, repositories, raw Cypher, transactions, hydration, drivers and read-model projections.

### `AccessMode` (type)

Session routing for a statement: 'READ' (replica-capable) or 'WRITE' (primaries). Where a query path leaves routing open, the facade's defaultRouting (itself defaulting to 'READ') decides; ConnectionProvider#run defaults to 'WRITE'.

_source: driver/types.ts_

### `BatchStatementError` (interface)

A single failed statement within a batch.

_source: transaction/errors.ts_

### `Builder` (class)

Fluent Cypher query builder. A statement-based builder: every `match()` / `create()` / `merge()` call starts a new statement segment; where clauses accumulate against the current segment and are flushed into it when the next segment starts or when `build()` is called. All user values are passed as query parameters - the generated query contains only aliases. The one exception is `RawExpression` property values (NTS-460), which render verbatim into patterns; bind the values they reference via `param(name, value)`.

_source: query/builder.ts_

### `BulkChunk` (interface)

The result of one chunk: the rows attempted and the hydrated created/merged entities, in row order

_source: services/query/bulk.service.ts_

### `BulkOptions` (interface)

_source: services/query/bulk.service.ts_

### `BulkService` (class)

Bulk CREATE and MERGE via UNWIND: one managed write transaction per chunk, one UNWIND statement per transaction, rows validated and reduced to property maps exactly like the single-create / merge paths

_source: services/query/bulk.service.ts_

### `Collection` (class)

An iterable wrapper over an array of entities (parity with neode's Collection): reads like an array, serialises through toJson().

_source: collection.ts_

### `ConnectionOptions` (interface)

Options a Neode instance accepts alongside its ConnectionProvider.

_source: driver/types.ts_

### `ConnectionProvider` (interface)

The connection port implemented by every backend.

_source: driver/types.ts_

### `CursorPage` (interface)

Cursor/keyset result — items are returned ascending either way

_source: services/query/paginate.service.ts_

### `CursorPaginateOptions` (interface)

Keyset/cursor pagination on a temporal (or other comparable) property: paginate(model, filter, { limit, orderBy?, after?, before? })

_source: services/query/paginate.service.ts_

### `CypherOptions` (interface)

Options for the unified raw query entry, `Neode#cypher`.

_source: driver/types.ts_

### `Direction` (const)

Direction of a relationship pattern. Accepts the legacy case-insensitive 'IN' / 'OUT' / 'BOTH' spellings anywhere a direction is taken.

_source: query/direction.ts_

### `EventType` (const)

Lifecycle events emitted by Neode (facade) and TransactionalService (work performed inside an open transaction). Subscribe with `neode.on(EventType.NODE_CREATED, handler)`, unsubscribe with `neode.off(...)`. Handlers receive the affected value as their only argument: | Event | Emitted by | Payload | |------------------------|-------------------------------------|--------------------| | NODE_CREATED | create(), save() when the merge created the node | hydrated entity | | NODE_UPDATED | save() when the merge matched an existing node | hydrated entity | | NODE_MERGED | reserved (mergeOn) | — | | NODE_DELETED | delete() | deleted entity | | RELATIONSHIP_CREATED | relate() with forceCreate | GraphRelationship | | RELATIONSHIP_MERGED | relate() (MERGE, the default) | GraphRelationship | | RELATIONSHIP_UPDATED | reserved | — | | RELATIONSHIP_DELETED | reserved (detach) | — | | QUERY_EXECUTED | every statement run through the | QueryExecutedEvent | | | instance's connection (raw + | | | | service queries, inside and outside | | | | transactions) | | Events are emitted synchronously on an EventEmitter scoped to the Neode instance.

_source: common/events.ts_

### `FindManyAndCountOptions` (interface)

findManyAndCount() options — they trim the data read only; `total` always counts the whole filter (Prisma parity)

_source: services/query/paginate.service.ts_

### `GraphNode` (interface)

A node value in a normalized shape, as returned in result records.

_source: driver/types.ts_

### `GraphRelationship` (interface)

A relationship value in a normalized shape, as returned in result records.

_source: driver/types.ts_

### `hasProjectedProperties` (function)

True when any property of the model projects a read-model value

_source: projection/projection.ts_

### `hydrate` (function)

Hydrate a raw query result (as returned by readCypher/writeCypher or Builder#execute) into typed entities: each record's `alias` column is the node, any other column feeds eager relationship hydration (neode's Factory.hydrate)

_source: hydrate.ts_

### `hydrateFirst` (function)

Hydrate the first record of a raw query result, or undefined when the result set is empty (neode's Factory.hydrateFirst)

_source: hydrate.ts_

### `hydrateProjection` (function)

Hydrate one row of a projection read (NTS-135/136/137/138). The RETURN map projection (projectionNode) carries the node properties inline with the identity markers and eager relationship values — the shape hydrateNode understands, so projected values land on the entity through the regular property hydration switch. This pass then post-processes the projected kinds: - full-entity

_source: projection/hydrate.ts_

### `instrumentConnectionProvider` (function)

Instrument a provider transparently: property reads the wrapper doesn't satisfy — duck-typed introspection such as `connection.database` on the neo4j provider — forward to the inner provider, so consumers holding `Neode#getConnection()` see through the instrumentation.

_source: driver/instrumented.ts_

### `jsonSafe` (function)

JSON-safe serialisation for raw query values: converts the driver class instances that survive value normalisation (Integer, temporal types, Point, Path) and bigints into structures that survive JSON.stringify, recursing through arrays and plain objects. Everything else passes through unchanged.

_source: driver/json-safe.ts_

### `jsonSafeRecord` (function)

A QueryRecord whose values are JSON-safe (the rows of `Neode#cypher`).

_source: driver/json-safe.ts_

### `knn` (function)

k-nearest-neighbour search over a vector index, returning hydrated entities with their similarity score, best match first. With the default `auto` mode the Cypher 25 `SEARCH` clause is attempted first and the queryNodes procedure is used as a fallback; when the backend supports neither a combined error is raised.

_source: services/query/knn.service.ts_

### `KnnMode` (type)

Which query form to use for the kNN search

_source: services/query/knn.service.ts_

### `LabelPredicate` (class)

A label predicate: `alias:Label` (several labels require all of them), shared by `whereLabel` (`WHERE n:Completed`) and `orderByLabel` (`ORDER BY n:Completed DESC`).

_source: query/label-predicate.ts_

### `ManyAndCount` (interface)

Non-paginated `{ items, total }` read (Prisma's findManyAndCount)

_source: services/query/paginate.service.ts_

### `Neo4jConnectionProvider` (class)

ConnectionProvider over a neo4j-driver `Driver` (Bolt): Neo4j Community/Enterprise, Aura, Memgraph, or `relate serve`. Result values are normalised out of driver types (Node, Relationship, Integer, temporal, Point) into the plain GraphNode/GraphRelationship shapes; driver errors are mapped through the typed error taxonomy.

_source: driver/neo4j-connection-provider.ts_

### `OffsetPaginateOptions` (interface)

Property -> direction pagination (the classic form): paginate(model, filter, { page, limit, order? })

_source: services/query/paginate.service.ts_

### `OrderSpec` (type)

Ordering spec, matching neode's all() forms: - `'name'` - order by one property ascending - `['name', 'age']` - order by several properties - `{ name: 'DESC' }` - property -> direction map - `[{ name: 'DESC' }, { age: 'ASC' }]` - list of property -> direction maps - `{ field: 'name', order: 'DESC' }` - two-arg (key, direction) descriptor

_source: query/order-spec.ts_

### `Page` (interface)

Offset/page result

_source: services/query/paginate.service.ts_

### `PaginateOptions` (type)

The union of the two pagination modes PaginateService accepts — the options shape (page vs cursor) selects the mode.

_source: services/query/paginate.service.ts_

### `PaginateService` (class)

Pagination helpers. Two modes, selected by the options shape: - `{ page, limit, order? }` — offset pagination over two autocommit reads (data + COUNT), returning { items, total, page, limit, totalPages } - `{ limit, orderBy?, after?/before? }` — keyset pagination on a temporal property (`WHERE this.createdAt > datetime($cursor)`), returning { items, nextCursor, hasMore }

_source: services/query/paginate.service.ts_

### `projectionNode` (function)

The RETURN map projection for a model's read query: all properties, the hydration identity markers, full-entity eager relationships and every projected property — one query per read.

_source: projection/projection.ts_

### `ProjectionService` (class)

Read service for models with projected properties (NTS-135/136/137/138): the same match / where surface as the plain query services, but the RETURN map projection carries every projected value — related subsets, counts, exists, label predicates, expressions — in one query per read. NTS-145: object values on

_source: projection/projection.service.ts_

### `Property` (class)

A property in a SET clause: `property operator $param` or, inline in a pattern, `property: $param`. With `isRaw`, the value renders verbatim (an inline Cypher expression, NTS-460) instead of a parameter reference.

_source: query/property.ts_

### `QueryExecutedEvent` (interface)

Payload of QUERY_EXECUTED, emitted once per executed statement.

_source: common/events.ts_

### `QueryOutput` (interface)

A query result, independent of the underlying client.

_source: driver/types.ts_

### `QueryParams` (type)

A map of Cypher parameter names to values, bound into the statement — values never render into the query text itself.

_source: driver/types.ts_

### `QueryRecord` (interface)

One row of a query result.

_source: driver/types.ts_

### `QuerySummary` (interface)

Metadata for one executed statement: write counters and (when the statement is prefixed with EXPLAIN / PROFILE) the server's plan.

_source: driver/types.ts_

### `RawExpression` (class)

A raw Cypher expression used as an inline pattern property value (NTS-460): rendered verbatim into the pattern — `{ prop: <expression> }` — instead of being bound as a parameter. Variable references (`row.answers`), server-side calls (`datetime()`) and parameter references (`$name`, bound via `Builder#param`) are all legal; the expression must never interpolate data.

_source: query/expressions.ts_

### `RelateConnectionProvider` (class)

ConnectionProvider over the embedded Relate engine (@relate/relate) — in-process, no Bolt server. The engine is a soft dependency, loaded at construction time; the client shapes are structural so it stays that way.

_source: driver/relate.ts_

### `Repository` (class)

Active-record style data-access repository for one registered model — the TypeORM-parity surface, obtained via `neode.getRepository(Entity)` or the

_source: repository/index.ts_

### `requireRelateClient` (function)

Resolve the Relate client module and native library. The client is not yet published to npm, so it is loaded from disk: 1. `RELATE_CLIENT_PATH` env var, or 2. the sibling `relate` repository checkout (`../relate/clients/javascript`) The native library location is passed through via `RELATE_LIB` (see the Relate client's loader) — detected automatically here when a sibling repository checkout exists.

_source: driver/relate.ts_

### `Runner` (interface)

Anything able to run statements in its scope (autocommit or transaction).

_source: driver/types.ts_

### `ScoredEntity` (interface)

A hydrated entity with the relevance score of the index that matched it

_source: services/query/search.service.ts_

### `search` (function)

Full-text search over a full-text index (`CALL db.index.fulltext.queryNodes`), returning hydrated entities with their relevance score, best match first. The query string is bound as a parameter, so Lucene syntax characters in it are still parsed as such — pass user text through `toFulltextQuery` first.

_source: services/query/search.service.ts_

### `StreamOptions` (interface)

lazy() options — the keyset walk behind cursor pagination

_source: services/query/paginate.service.ts_

### `toCollection` (function)

Hydrate a raw query result into a Collection (neode's Factory.hydrate return shape)

_source: hydrate.ts_

### `toDirection` (function)

Normalise a direction given in any supported spelling to a Direction. Unknown values fall back to BOTH (the most permissive direction), matching neode's behaviour of never throwing on a bad direction.

_source: query/direction.ts_

### `toJson` (function)

Convert an entity into a JSON friendly object: plain properties (hidden and structural properties skipped), `_id` (elementId when the model carries an internal id property) and `_labels` (the schema's labels). Eagerly loaded relationships are serialised recursively.

_source: serialise.ts_

### `TransactionalService` (class)

The INeode surface scoped to one open transaction: every read/write runs through the TransactionHandle opened by `Neode#beginTransaction` until its commit/rollback, with the facade's model methods (create, merge, relate, …) mirrored inside that scope.

_source: transaction/transactional.service.ts_

### `TransactionError` (class)

Thrown by Neode.batch() when any statement of the batch fails and the transaction is rolled back (port of neode's TransactionError): - `errors` — per-statement error aligned with the input batch, null where the statement succeeded - `results` — results of the statements that succeeded before the failure - `details` — the failed statements only ({ index, query, params, error })

_source: transaction/errors.ts_

### `TransactionHandle` (interface)

An explicit transaction: statements run in scope until commit/rollback.

_source: driver/types.ts_

### `valueToJson` (function)

Convert a single property value into its JSON friendly shape.

_source: serialise.ts_

### `WhereNull` (class)

An `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` predicate on a property, rendered by toString() — the value of `Builder.whereNull` / `whereNotNull`.

_source: query/where-null.ts_

## Schema management

Indexes, constraints, full-text and vector indexes, schema inspection and drift workflow.

### `ApplySchemaDiffOptions` (interface)

Options for applySchemaDrift.

_source: services/schema/drift.service.ts_

### `applySchemaDrift` (function)

Apply the missing objects of a drift idempotently — every CREATE carries IF NOT EXISTS. Stale objects are only dropped with `dropStale: true` (dropping is destructive). Mismatched objects are never applied automatically. Each statement is reported with a SchemaResult, following the SchemaService pattern (NTS-450).

_source: services/schema/drift.service.ts_

### `formatSchemaDrift` (function)

Human-readable multi-line drift report, grouped by action (missing / stale / mismatched), one line per object plus its fix statement. Pure function — no database access (NTS-450).

_source: services/schema/drift.service.ts_

### `FulltextIndexDefinition` (interface)

A full-text index to keep installed on the database

_source: services/schema/fulltext.service.ts_

### `fulltextIndexName` (function)

_source: services/schema/fulltext.service.ts_

### `FulltextIndexService` (class)

Installs/drops the given full-text index definitions, following the same result-reporting pattern as SchemaService

_source: services/schema/fulltext.service.ts_

### `InspectOptions` (interface)

Which objects count as "declared" for the inspection: pass the full-text/vector index definitions and the enterprise flag your installSchema call used, so the diff is not polluted by false "extra" entries.

_source: services/schema/inspect.service.ts_

### `inspectSchema` (function)

Read the installed schema (SHOW CONSTRAINTS / SHOW INDEXES) and diff it against the declared schema

_source: services/schema/inspect.service.ts_

### `SchemaDiff` (interface)

The declared-vs-installed diff for one schema family (constraints or indexes): the raw object lists plus the names that only appear on one side.

_source: services/schema/inspect.service.ts_

### `schemaDrift` (function)

Structured schema drift (NTS-450): the declared-vs-installed inspection of constraints and every index kind (range/text/fulltext/vector), with the exact fix statement per entry. Cheap and drift-never-throws: drift is data, not an error — failing a CI run on a non-empty diff is the caller's job.

_source: services/schema/drift.service.ts_

### `SchemaDrift` (interface)

_source: services/schema/drift.service.ts_

### `SchemaDriftEntry` (interface)

One drifted schema object: what it is, where it lives, and the exact statement(s) that would resolve the drift (NTS-450)

_source: services/schema/drift.service.ts_

### `SchemaDriftGroup` (interface)

Drift of one schema family (constraints or indexes), grouped by action

_source: services/schema/drift.service.ts_

### `SchemaInspection` (interface)

The full inspectSchema result: constraint and index diffs against the declared models.

_source: services/schema/inspect.service.ts_

### `SchemaObject` (interface)

One constraint or index as inspected from the database (SHOW CONSTRAINTS / SHOW INDEXES).

_source: services/schema/inspect.service.ts_

### `VectorIndexDefinition` (interface)

A vector index to keep installed on the database

_source: services/schema/vector.service.ts_

### `vectorIndexName` (function)

_source: services/schema/vector.service.ts_

### `VectorIndexService` (class)

Installs/drops the given vector index definitions, following the same result-reporting pattern as SchemaService

_source: services/schema/vector.service.ts_

## Testing & ops

wipe()/testId() test utilities, factory seeding, connectivity checks and Cypher-script helpers.

### `ConnectivityConfig` (interface)

The connection config the checks run against — the shape fromEnv() produces (uri + auth + driver config + database).

_source: ops/verify-connectivity.ts_

### `ConnectivityTimeoutError` (class)

Rejected by waitUntilReachable when the deadline passes.

_source: ops/verify-connectivity.ts_

### `FactoryBuilder` (class)

Chainable factory builder (NTS-444): seed fake data through the library's normal create/relate services, so validation, defaults, timestamps and relationship logic all apply. neode.factory('User') .count(10) .with('posts', { count: 2, properties: { title: 'Seeded' } }) .create({ role: 'admin' }) Precedence on create: explicit value > `default` > `fake`. Unique properties with a `fake` generator are retried until the values are distinct within one batch (app-level check) — across runs the user's fake fn must be DB-safe (e.g. random UUIDs). An override on a unique property applies to the first row; later rows fake distinct values around it. `.make()` resolves the same properties but returns unsaved instances; `.has(otherFactory, relationshipName)` composes another factory's output onto every created instance through the explicit relate path.

_source: services/factory.service.ts_

### `FactoryWithSpec` (interface)

Options for one `.with()` call on a factory builder (NTS-444)

_source: services/factory.service.ts_

### `runCypherScript` (function)

Run every statement of a script sequentially against a runner. Stops at (rejects on) the first failing statement.

_source: ops/cypher-script.ts_

### `RunCypherScriptOptions` (interface)

Options for runCypherScript.

_source: ops/cypher-script.ts_

### `runSeeders` (function)

Run seeders in order against one Neode instance.

_source: testing/seeder.ts_

### `seededRandom` (function)

A deterministic PRNG (mulberry32) for reproducible fixtures (NTS-167): seed it once and use it inside property `fake` generators — the same seed produces the same sequence, so seeded fixtures stay stable across runs. const random = seededRandom(42)

_source: testing/random.ts_

### `Seeder` (class)

Base class for seeders (NTS-167): `runSeeders()` calls seed() once per seeder, in order. Write idempotently inside seed() — `neode.mergeOn(model, match, set)` or `neode.merge(model, properties)` MERGE on the node's merge fields — so rerunning the runner updates instead of duplicating.

_source: testing/seeder.ts_

### `splitCypherStatements` (function)

Split a script's contents into statements. Semicolons split statements except when they appear inside: - single- or double-quoted string literals (backslash escapes honoured), - backtick-quoted identifiers (`` `a``b` `` doubling honoured), - `--` and `//` line comments, and `/*` block comments (to the closer). Chunks that hold nothing but whitespace and comments are dropped, and each remaining statement is trimmed. Comments that belong to a statement are kept — they are legal Cypher.

_source: ops/cypher-script.ts_

### `testId` (function)

Unique identifier for test data — `test-<timestamp>-<random>` by default, safe as a property value (letters, digits and hyphens only).

_source: testing/test-id.ts_

### `verifyConnectivity` (function)

Check that a database is reachable right now, using a throwaway driver constructed from the config (closed again afterwards). Note the check runs with whatever connectionTimeout the config carries — the driver's default applies otherwise.

_source: ops/verify-connectivity.ts_

### `waitUntilReachable` (function)

Retry verifyConnectivity with exponential-ish backoff until the database is reachable or the timeout elapses (then: ConnectivityTimeoutError).

_source: ops/verify-connectivity.ts_

### `WaitUntilReachableOptions` (interface)

Backoff and probe options for waitUntilReachable — every field optional.

_source: ops/verify-connectivity.ts_

### `wipe` (function)

Wipe the database clean for a test run: DETACH DELETE every node, then drop every constraint and index the database currently has. Standalone on purpose — SchemaService derives DROP statements from the registered models, while wipe() discovers them from the database itself (small duplication of its statement shapes, accepted). Index drops are best-effort: built-in indexes (e.g. the token lookup store on real servers) cannot be dropped and are ignored.

_source: testing/wipe.ts_

### `WipeTarget` (type)

A Runner, or any facade exposing one (e.g. Neode — matched structurally to avoid importing the service here).

_source: testing/wipe.ts_

## Errors

Typed error taxonomy and driver-error classification.

### `classifyError` (function)

Map a raw driver/engine error to the typed taxonomy (NTS-129): constraint violations → ConstraintViolationError, transient codes and retryable-flagged failures → TransientError. Everything else — unknown shapes and already-typed errors — passes through untouched.

_source: errors/classify.ts_

### `ConstraintViolationError` (class)

A unique-constraint violation, raised on `merge()`/`create()` flows that race an existing node. `label`/`property` are parsed from the database message when it names them (Neo4j does; the embedded Relate engine only names the constraint), and stay undefined otherwise.

_source: errors/constraint-violation.ts_

### `isTransientError` (function)

Type guard for classified transient errors.

_source: errors/classify.ts_

### `NeodeError` (class)

Base class of the typed error taxonomy (NTS-129). Typed errors are produced by `classifyError`, which wraps the raw driver/engine error — the original is preserved as `cause`.

_source: errors/neode-error.ts_

### `OptimisticLockError` (class)

Raised when an optimistic-lock check (NTS-158) matched zero rows: the `@Version` property the instance was hydrated with no longer matches the stored one — the node was modified or deleted by another transaction. This is NOT a transient failure: retrying without reloading will fail again. Reload the entity (find / findById / a fresh get) and re-apply the change. The stable `name` lets retry helpers exclude it from transient- retry classification.

_source: errors/optimistic-lock.ts_

### `RelationNotLoadedError` (class)

Raised when strict relation access is on (setStrictRelationAccess) and a relationship property the load spec did not request is read off a hydrated entity (NTS-155). The message names the exact fix: request the relation in the load spec (`with`) or load it on the instance.

_source: errors/relation-not-loaded.ts_

### `TransientError` (class)

A transient failure (`Neo.TransientError.*` codes, or the driver's / engine's own `retryable` verdict): retrying the operation may succeed. `isRetryable` is baked in by the code classification — a TransientError is only ever created for a retryable failure.

_source: errors/transient.ts_

## Core

Collection, serialisation and other shared exports.

### `fromEnv` (function)

Load a .env file (dotenv does not clobber variables already set in process.env), map the NEO4J_* variables to a connection config and construct the neo4j driver. `driverConfig` — anything neo4j.driver accepts, e.g. `disableLosslessIntegers: true` — is forwarded verbatim, merged over the env-derived values.

_source: from-env.ts_

### `setStrictRelationAccess` (function)

Enable or disable strict relation access. Off by default: neode-style code relies on reading an unloaded relationship as `undefined` — flip it on once every relationship you read is in the load spec (or eager).

_source: strict-relation-access.ts_

### `toFulltextQuery` (function)

Sanitise free user text into a safe full-text query string: Lucene syntax characters and uppercase boolean operators stripped, terms lowercased and capped at `maxTerms` (default 12). Pass user text through this before `search()` / `Repository#search` — binding the string as a parameter stops Cypher injection, but the Lucene parser still 500s on syntax characters (`(`, `"`, `*`, `AND`, …).

_source: services/index-support/lucene.ts_

### `ValidationDetail` (interface)

One failed check, shaped like a Joi detail

_source: validation/validation-error.ts_

### `ValidationError` (class)

_source: validation/validation-error.ts_

## Schema reference

Every field of the map-based schema interfaces, with its type and JSDoc
description. This section is extracted from src/meta/schema-definition.interface.ts,
so new fields (e.g. upcoming schema options) appear here automatically.

### PropertyDefinition

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `PropertyTypeName` |  |
| `description` | `string` (optional) | Free-text explanation of the property for LLM-agent-facing ontology emission (NTS-445): surfaced by `ontology()` / `ontologyMarkdown()`. |
| `array` | `boolean` (optional) |  |
| `default` | `DefaultValue` (optional) |  |
| `primary` | `boolean` (optional) |  |
| `fulltext` | `boolean` (optional) | Include in the model's full-text search index (NTS-436). |
| `unique` | `boolean | string[]` (optional) | boolean: single-property unique constraint. string[]: composite unique covering exactly the listed properties (NTS-140) — declared on one property, the array is the full composite. |
| `onCreateSet` | `boolean` (optional) |  |
| `onMatchSet` | `boolean` (optional) |  |
| `alwaysSet` | `boolean` (optional) |  |
| `createdAt` | `boolean` (optional) | Server-side timestamp (NTS-165): stamped with `datetime()` once on create — the map-API form of `@CreatedAt`. |
| `updatedAt` | `boolean` (optional) | Server-side timestamp (NTS-165): stamped with `datetime()` on create and on every write — the map-API form of `@UpdatedAt`. |
| `version` | `boolean` (optional) | Optimistic locking (NTS-158): the integer property every write keeps in sync — stamped 0 on create, incremented by 1 on every write addressed to the node, and checked with `WHERE n.version = $expected` when the instance carries the version it was hydrated with (a mismatch throws `OptimisticLockError`). The map-API form of `@Version`. |
| `required` | `boolean` (optional) |  |
| `hidden` | `boolean` (optional) |  |
| `protected` | `boolean` (optional) |  |
| `readonly` | `boolean` (optional) |  |
| `index` | `boolean | string[]` (optional) | boolean: single-property index. string[]: composite index covering exactly the listed properties (NTS-140). |
| `exists` | `boolean` (optional) |  |
| `typed` | `boolean` (optional) | Opt in to a property-type constraint generated from the declared type (NTS-141): `REQUIRE n.prop IS :: STRING`. |
| `vector` | `VectorConfig` (optional) | Declare a vector index over the property (NTS-447): created by `installSchema()` with the deterministic `vectorIndexName()` naming and dropped by `dropSchema()`. |
| `transform` | `TransformConfig` (optional) | Property value transforms (NTS-449): `in` converts the user value into its stored form before validation on every write path (create / update / merge / bulk writes), `out` converts the stored form back at hydration on read. See TransformConfig. |
| `coalesce` | `string | string[]` (optional) | Read-side fallbacks applied at hydration when the stored/projected value is null or absent (NTS-139, the Zod `.catch()` analogue): a literal, or sibling property names whose first non-null value wins. |
| `fake` | `() => unknown` (optional) | Per-property fake data generator (NTS-444): user-supplied, no faker dependency. Invoked by factory seeding (and the create path) when neither an explicit value nor `default` applies — precedence on create is explicit value > `default` > `fake`, and generated values are validated like any other write. |

### RelationshipDefinition

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `'relationship' | 'relationships' | 'node' | 'nodes'` |  |
| `description` | `string` (optional) | Free-text explanation of the relationship for LLM-agent-facing ontology emission (NTS-445): surfaced by `ontology()` / `ontologyMarkdown()`. |
| `relationship` | `string` | Neo4j relationship type, e.g. 'KNOWS' |
| `direction` | `string` | 'in' | 'out' | 'both' (case-insensitive, invalid falls back to both) |
| `target` | `string` | Name of the model this relationship points at |
| `properties` | `Record<string, PropertyTypeName | PropertyDefinition>` (optional) | shortcut: edge properties are parsed but not wired yet — needs a generated relationship entity; add when edge-property saves are needed |
| `eager` | `boolean` (optional) |  |

### SchemaDefinition

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `labels` | `string[]` (optional) |  |
| `description` | `string` (optional) | Free-text explanation of the model for LLM-agent-facing ontology emission (NTS-445): surfaced by `ontology()` / `ontologyMarkdown()`. |
| `[key: string]` | `SchemaDefinitionEntry | string[] | string | undefined` |  |

## Agent ontology API

Every registered model — whether defined with decorators or the map API — can be
emitted as an agent-readable ontology. Descriptions come from the
`description` field on the model, property and relationship definitions.

### `ontology` (function)

Build an agent-readable ontology over ALL registered models (NTS-445): entities with their labels, descriptions, properties and relationships, pulled from the shared metadata registry the map API and decorators both write into. Purely synchronous, no database connection required.

_source: meta/ontology.ts_

### `ontologyMarkdown` (function)

Render `ontology()` as prompt-ready markdown (NTS-445): a heading per entity, bullet lists per property and relationship, descriptions included where declared.

_source: meta/ontology.ts_

```ts
import { ontology, ontologyMarkdown } from 'neode'

// Ground a Text2Cypher prompt: hand the LLM the live schema, not its
// training-data memory of it.
const systemPrompt = [
  'You write Cypher against the graph described below.',
  'Only use the entities, properties and relationships listed.',
  '',
  ontologyMarkdown(),
].join('\n')

// Or expose it over MCP as a resource / tool result:
server.resource('graph-ontology', () => ontologyMarkdown())
server.tool('describe-ontology', async () => ({ content: [{ type: 'text', text: JSON.stringify(ontology()) }] }))
```
